provenance.rule: Every scored question and every setup turn is the EXACT text of a real logged user question, taken from the CSV after decoding, including typos, casing and punctuation. v4 reads these strings from the CSV by log id rather than transcribing them, and validation compares every scored and setup question against the decoded CSV — not merely the corrected ones.
provenance.tab_field: The `tab` value is the section the question was actually asked in, taken from the log. It is the routing expectation unless `routing_note` says otherwise.
provenance.source_log_id_rule: Every scored case carries source_log_id: the id of the exact source-log row its question was read from. Question text and tab alone do NOT identify that row — 25 scored cases match more than one log row on both. Selection is deterministic and recorded per case in source_log_id_rule: S1 the id already named in the case text_source; S2 for a follow-up, the continuation of the recovered setup chain, i.e. the earliest matching row after the last setup turn; S3 the only matching row; S4 the earliest of several identical rows. Validation requires the exact triple (source_log_id, tab, decoded question) to match the source CSV, requires every selected id to be unique across scored cases, and fails on a missing, duplicate, or nonexistent id or on any text or tab mismatch. Setup turns carry and are validated on their own log_id the same way. source_log_id is provenance for the question text only. It is NEVER ground truth: the logged response, SQL, row count and error of that row are historical and are not the expected answer for the baseline run.

coverage_evidence_rule: RECONCILED. GC-045 and GC-121 probe Decision 13's outside-coverage branch. The condition was established against the local 2026-08-16 artifact, which is NOT deployment-aligned. Re-establishing it from the assistant's own explanatory prose is NOT an independent check and is forbidden. What would count as live-era evidence: raw returned rows from the live response showing the resolved entity's actual maximum covered period, or a deployment-aligned coverage artifact obtained without additional production contact. AN EMPTY ROW SET ALONE IS NOT EVIDENCE — it cannot distinguish outside coverage from any other cause. If no such evidence is available at run time, GC-045 and GC-121 are INCONCLUSIVE for that branch. ground_truth_rule: Any data-condition claim must come from independently reviewable rows plus a correct entity and query resolution — including agency type. It is never inferred from the prose response being tested. If the condition cannot be established, the case is inconclusive.

mechanical_check_vocabulary.rows_count: Compare the number of data rows returned. Operands: op (eq|gte|lte), value (integer). Evidence: the returned rows, per capture_state_rule.row_dependent_operations. A CAPTURED result holding zero rows is a determinate count of 0, not an inconclusive: under the scoring rule a product timeout or error is a FAIL under Decision 13 or 15. INCONCLUSIVE only where the rows field was not captured; a missing rows capture can never pass an expectation of zero rows. Whether SQL was captured does not affect this operation.
mechanical_check_vocabulary.sql_limit_eq: The OUTERMOST row limit governing the rows returned to the user equals the operand. Operands: value (integer). Evidence: the generated SQL only, per capture_state_rule.sql_dependent_operations — this operation is scoreable whether or not any rows were captured, and is inconclusive when the sql field is missing or empty. This is NOT the first occurrence of the word LIMIT. Contract: comments (-- and /* */) and quoted literals and identifiers are removed first, so LIMIT text inside them is never read; the governing limit is the LIMIT at parenthesis depth 0, which excludes every limit inside a CTE body, a subquery or a derived table. In the SQLite form LIMIT <offset>, <count> the governing row count is <count>. VERDICTS: pass if a depth-0 limit exists and equals the operand; FAIL if a depth-0 limit exists and differs, and FAIL if the statement has no depth-0 limit at all, because the outer query then returns unlimited rows; INCONCLUSIVE if no SQL was captured, if the parentheses are unbalanced, if more than one depth-0 limit is found, or if the limit is not a literal integer (for example a bound parameter). A limit that cannot be established safely is never guessed.
mechanical_check_vocabulary.result_entities_include: The distinct entities in the returned rows include every literal entity named. Operands: entities (array of literals in canonical form). Evidence: the returned rows, per capture_state_rule.row_dependent_operations. A CAPTURED result holding zero rows returned zero entities and therefore FAILS this check; it is not inconclusive. Identity, priority, conflicts and the remaining verdicts are governed by entity_identity_rule.
mechanical_check_vocabulary.result_entities_count: Count distinct entities in the returned rows. Operands: op (eq|gte|lte), value (integer). Evidence: the returned rows, per capture_state_rule.row_dependent_operations. A CAPTURED result holding zero rows is a determinate count of 0 and is compared with the operand like any other count. Identity, priority, conflicts and the remaining verdicts are governed by entity_identity_rule.

mechanical_rule: An expectation is mechanical ONLY if it carries a check_op from the vocabulary above plus LITERAL operands — arrays of named entities, or integers. A description a human must resolve is not an operand; such expectations are semantic. A keyword is never proof of meaning, and a result composition is never proof that a filter was or was not applied.

scoring.expectation_level: Every expectation carries its own verdict: pass, fail, inconclusive, or not applicable.
scoring.case_level: Derived from the expectation verdicts; it never replaces them.
scoring.semantic_verdicts: Left BLANK by Claude. Codex makes every semantic judgement from the saved responses after the run. Claude assembles evidence and runs mechanical checks only. Each semantic verdict records the relevant response passage and a one-sentence reason.
scoring.inconclusive: Reserved for failures of the measurement, or where the frozen rule does not permit a confident judgement. Never stretched into a pass or a fail.
scoring.product_failure: A product timeout or error is a FAIL under Decision 13 or 15 — never inconclusive.
scoring.no_retry: A content or semantic failure is never retried. A transport failure (rate limit, expired token, CAPTCHA) may be retried once as infrastructure recovery, but BOTH attempts and the reason are saved and the first is never silently replaced.
scoring.not_applicable: A conditional expectation whose condition does not hold is recorded not applicable, and is excluded from the case verdict and from per-decision totals.
scoring.mechanical_three_state: A mechanical check returns pass, fail, or inconclusive. Inconclusive means the capture does not carry the evidence the operation needs — it is never rounded to a pass or a fail. Every mechanical operation in this set has an explicit inconclusive condition stated in its vocabulary entry.

reporting_rule: The final baseline report MUST state that Decision 13's true-zero branch was not measured, and MUST NOT report Decision 13 as fully covered.

entity_identity_rule.purpose: Defines how an actual captured row becomes the canonical identity used by result_entities_include and result_entities_count. Written against real response-row shapes recovered from the source log, not invented ones. v4 fixtures assumed a single `entity` field; no such field exists in the live transport.
entity_identity_rule.transport: A result carries columns: string[] and rows: Record<string, unknown>[], each row keyed by the column name the generated SQL produced. Identity, when present at all, is spread across several of those columns.
entity_identity_rule.column_roles_evidence: Derived by parsing the outer select list of 6,614 successful logged queries across all tabs. These are the only identity-bearing column names that actually occur, and each array is in priority order. Measured on the same corpus: NO observed result shape carries two columns of the same role, so the conflict rule is a guard against a latent implementation defect rather than a frequent condition.
entity_identity_rule.canonical_form: Name, ST, type=Type — for example "Albuquerque, NM, type=City". Name is the name-role value with surrounding whitespace trimmed and internal whitespace collapsed, compared case-insensitively; when the resolved type is County a single trailing " County" is stripped, because county agencies are returned as "Lewis County" while a city may legitimately be named "Pocomoke City". ST is the state-role value uppercased. Type is the type-role value title-cased.
entity_identity_rule.time_series_collapse: Identity is built ONLY from role columns. Every other column — year, month, counts, rates — is ignored, so repeated time-series rows for one entity resolve to one identity and are counted once.
entity_identity_rule.ori_rule: Where an ori column is present it is a complete discriminator and participates in the identity tuple, so two rows differing only by ori are two entities. ori is not by itself converted into a canonical name; name, state and type roles supply the name.
entity_identity_rule.scoring_result_entities_count: Count distinct identities over the chosen role columns. A CAPTURED result holding zero rows is a determinate count of 0. INCONCLUSIVE where the rows field was not captured, where a nonempty result carries no name role and no ori, where same-role columns conflict, or where any row is UNRESOLVED — a row carrying no usable value in the chosen name column. An unresolved row is never silently dropped and is never rescued by a lower-priority column.
entity_identity_rule.scoring_result_entities_include: A CAPTURED result holding zero rows returned no entities and FAILS. An absent capture is INCONCLUSIVE. Otherwise, per expected literal, three states. INCONCLUSIVE if a nonempty result carries no identity role at all, if same-role columns conflict, or if any row is UNRESOLVED because the chosen name column carries no usable value on it. If every component the literal names (name, state, type) is carried by the returned rows: PASS when some row matches all of them, FAIL when none does. If the rows carry only some of those components: FAIL when no row matches even on the components present, because absence is provable; INCONCLUSIVE when a row matches on the components present but a required component — typically agency type — is not carried, because a name-only match cannot separate a city from a same-named county. That asymmetry is deliberate: it is the trap that invalidated v2, where Kalamazoo City was matched against a Kalamazoo County row.
entity_identity_rule.pivoted_results: Some real results are wide: the entities appear in the COLUMN NAMES and not in any row value. GC-083's actual logged result has columns albuquerque_police_department_murders and bernalillo_county_sheriff_murders, and the state never appears anywhere in the result. Identity recovered from a column header would be a name invented by the evaluator, and the state could not be established at all. Such results are never scored by parsing column names. In v6 the four questions known to produce shapes like this — GC-075, GC-080, GC-083 and GC-084 — carry semantic expectations instead, so this branch now guards the remaining mechanical checks rather than describing their expected outcome.
entity_identity_rule.expected_literals_unchanged: The literal expected names in v4 are carried into v5 unchanged. The normalizer produces exactly these canonical identities from a row that carries the name, state and type roles.
entity_identity_rule.observed_shape_risk: RESOLVED IN v6 for the four predictable cases. Against the shapes these questions actually produced in the log: GC-081 carries ori, agency, state and type and remains a fully scoreable mechanical check; GC-115 and GC-116 carry city and state and remain scoreable mechanical distinct-count checks. GC-075 (offense, total), GC-080 (victims) and GC-083/GC-084 (pivoted) carried no identity role and would have scored inconclusive, so their expectations are now semantic with the same expected behaviour. The remaining mechanical entity checks are those whose known result shapes carry enough identity to score.
entity_identity_rule.identity_column_priority: Deterministic, result-wide, and WITHOUT FALLBACK. For each role the column_roles array is a PRIORITY ORDER, highest first. One column per role is chosen once for the whole result — the highest-priority role column present anywhere in it — and that exact column is then read for every row. Selection never depends on the key order of an individual row, and it never changes from row to row. If a row carries no usable value in the CHOSEN name column, that row is UNRESOLVED and the mechanical check is INCONCLUSIVE; the evaluator does not substitute a lower-priority same-role column for that row. This closes the v6 implementation, which selected the first POPULATED candidate per row and so silently fell back to a lower-priority column — reintroducing the row-by-row switching the rule exists to prevent.
entity_identity_rule.conflicting_identity_columns: Additional same-role columns are inspected ONLY to detect agreement or conflict. They are never used as fallback identity values. Where a row populates more than one column of a role, the normalized values are compared: agreement is harmless and the chosen column is used; ANY disagreement makes the check INCONCLUSIVE, never resolved by preferring whichever field appears first. Comparison uses the same normalization as the canonical form, so "Lewis County" in an agency column and "Lewis" in a county column agree for a county-type row.

capture_state_rule.principle: Each mechanical operation requires only the evidence it actually reads. No operation is inconclusive merely because unrelated evidence is missing, and no operation may be scored from evidence it does not read. This replaces v6's single rows-based rule, which was written as though it governed every mechanical operation and so contradicted sql_limit_eq.
capture_state_rule.row_dependent_operations: rows_count, result_entities_include and result_entities_count read the returned rows. Their evidence is CAPTURED when the response carried a rows field holding a list, EVEN IF THAT LIST IS EMPTY; it is NOT CAPTURED when the payload, the rows field, or its list type is absent. The distinction is load-bearing and must never collapse: a captured empty result is positive evidence that zero rows were returned, while an absent capture is a failure of the measurement. An absent rows capture is INCONCLUSIVE for these three operations and can never satisfy an expectation — including an expectation of zero rows. Implementations must test for the presence of the rows field, never read a missing field as an empty list. Whether SQL was captured is irrelevant to these three.
capture_state_rule.sql_dependent_operations: sql_limit_eq reads the generated SQL. Its evidence is CAPTURED when the response carried a non-empty sql field. A missing or empty sql field is INCONCLUSIVE for sql_limit_eq regardless of whether rows were captured. Conversely a captured sql field is fully scoreable even when no rows field was saved at all: the limit governing the result is a property of the query, not of the rows it happened to return.
capture_state_rule.no_unrelated_evidence: No operation may require unrelated evidence merely to become scoreable. A capture carrying SQL but no rows is scoreable by sql_limit_eq and inconclusive for the row-dependent operations; a capture carrying rows but no SQL is the exact reverse. Each verdict is decided only from the evidence its own operation names.
